Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

conclusion noun

a judgement reached by reasoning

also conclude, come to the conclusion, draw a conclusion, infer, I infer from what you say

classical

Cic. Att. 2.23.1: ex eō colligere poteris quantā occupātiōne distinear
Traupman 101: ex verbīs tuīs colligō (+ acc. & inf.)

colligō, colligere, collēgī, collēctum

verb, third conjugation; ex and the ablative, with an accusative and infinitive or an indirect question

conclude, infer (from)

Lewis & Short: “to gather, conclude, deduce, infer from what precedes (most freq. in Quint.)”. Latin draws the conclusion with a verb where English names it.

Other words

  • conclūdō, conclūdere, conclūsī, conclūsum — conclude, infer (in an argument)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.22: quō modō efficiātur conclūdāturque ratiō

    A term of logic and rhetoric; also “bring to an end, close”.

  • conclūsiō, conclūsiōnis f. — the conclusion of an argument

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.103 (Lewis & Short)

    In logic, what follows from the premises; also the closing part of a speech (Cic. de Or. 2.80).

Examples

  • numquam ante arbitror tē epistulam meam lēgisse nisi meā manū scrīptam. ex eō colligere poteris quantā occupātiōne distinear.

    I don’t think you have ever before read a letter of mine that was not in my own hand. From that you can conclude how busy I am.Cic. Att. 2.23.1

See also argument, decide, finally.
